title: Troubleshooting methodology
summary: Find faults systematically: symptom, evidence, hypothesis, test, repair and verification.

sections.heading: Evidence before conclusions
sections.body: Good troubleshooting is a method, not luck: understand the symptom, reproduce it, collect evidence from the process to the program, form one hypothesis that explains everything, test it, repair the root cause and verify the whole function.

sections.heading: Divide the signal path
sections.body: Each test halves the search space.
sections.diagram:
field device --> wiring --> terminal --> module --> input image --> program --> output
            measure here?            LED here?           tag here?

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body: Motor will not start: StartPB becomes TRUE (good), StopPB is FALSE at rest (bad), the Stop terminal shows 0 V with the button released: an NO block replaced the NC block.

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: Changing the program to 'make it work' (for example writing NOT StopPB) instead of repairing the hardware. The machine then loses its wire-break safety.

question.question: The input LED is ON but the PLC tag is FALSE. What do you check next?
options: The I/O mapping and module configuration
question.explanation: The field side works; the fault is between module and program.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting lab
sections.body: Find out why the conveyor will not start after panel maintenance.

sections.heading: Summary and troubleshooting note
sections.body:
Symptom, evidence, hypothesis, test, repair, verify: always in this order.

**Troubleshooting note:** In PLC Lab troubleshooting labs every guess is recorded; a correct first diagnosis earns full points.

checkpoint.question: What should a hypothesis explain?
checkpoint.explanation: One cause must explain all evidence.

checkpoint.question: What completes a repair?
checkpoint.explanation: Verification proves the fix and finds side effects.
